<!-- README.md is generated from README.Rmd. Please edit that file -->

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(peler)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

# GitHub removes inline SVG from a README, and a diagram saved without a theme has a
# transparent background, so pele's dark text would vanish in GitHub's dark mode. Here a
# diagram prints as a <picture> of two SVG files instead: pele's colours, and dark ones
# that GitHub picks in dark mode. A themed diagram paints its own background, so it gets
# one file. The method is registered in knitr's namespace because there R finds it before
# peler's own method.
dark <- pele_theme(
  bg = "#0d1117", fg = "#e6e4d9", muted = "#b7b5ac", line = "#cecdc3",
  surface = "#282726", surface_alt = "#343331", border = "#575653"
)
registerS3method("knit_print", "pele", envir = asNamespace("knitr"), function(x, options, ...) {
  file <- paste0("man/figures/README-", options$label, c(".svg", "-dark.svg"))
  pele_save(x, file[1])
  img <- sprintf('<img src="%s" alt="A %s diagram">', file[1], x$type)
  if (is.null(x$theme)) {
    pele_save(x, file[2], theme = dark)
    img <- sprintf(
      '<picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="%s">%s</picture>',
      file[2], img
    )
  }
  knitr::asis_output(paste0("\n", img, "\n"))
})
```

# peler

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/eli-daniels/peler/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/eli-daniels/peler/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

peler is an R port of [pele](https://github.com/obsidianmd/pele), the
[Mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org) renderer made by kepano at [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md).
All the rendering is pele's work. peler runs pele's JavaScript bundle in
[V8](https://cran.r-project.org/package=V8) and connects its SVG output to Quarto,
R Markdown, Shiny and image files.

This package will be updated as new versions of pele are released upstream.

For the diagram syntax, the supported diagram types and the theming variables,
read pele's own documentation at [pele.run](https://pele.run):

- [API](https://pele.run/api): render options and error handling
- [Theming](https://pele.run/theming): every CSS variable and class name
- [Security](https://pele.run/security): how pele handles untrusted diagram text

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("eli-daniels/peler")
```

## Quarto

Load peler in a setup chunk. After that, a `pele` chunk renders the Mermaid text it contains:

````markdown
---
title: "Release process"
format:
  html: default
  pdf: default
---

```{r}`r ''`
#| include: false
library(peler)
```

```{pele}`r ''`
#| label: release
#| echo: false
flowchart LR
  A[Commit] --> B{Tests pass?}
  B -->|yes| C[Release]
  B -->|no| D[Fix]
```
````

```{r}
#| label: release
#| echo: false
pele(r"(
flowchart LR
  A[Commit] --> B{Tests pass?}
  B -->|yes| C[Release]
  B -->|no| D[Fix]
)")
```

In HTML the diagram is inline SVG. In PDF it is a vector figure, and in Word a PNG.
R Markdown works the same way.

From an R chunk, call `pele()` on a string and print the result:

```{r}
#| label: hello
pele(c(
  "sequenceDiagram",
  "  Alice ->> Bob: Hello",
  "  Bob -->> Alice: Hi!"
))
```

## Diagrams from data

Mermaid is text, so R can write it. A data frame of flows becomes a Sankey diagram:

```{r}
#| label: sankey
flows <- data.frame(
  from = c("Screened", "Screened", "Enrolled", "Enrolled"),
  to = c("Enrolled", "Excluded", "Completed", "Withdrew"),
  n = c(120, 40, 95, 25)
)
pele(c("sankey", paste(flows$from, flows$to, flows$n, sep = ",")))
```

A summary of `airquality` becomes a bar chart:

```{r}
#| label: xychart
temp <- aggregate(Temp ~ Month, airquality, mean)
pele(c(
  "xychart",
  '  title "Mean temperature in New York, 1973"',
  sprintf("  x-axis [%s]", toString(month.abb[temp$Month])),
  '  y-axis "Degrees Fahrenheit" 50 --> 90',
  sprintf("  bar [%s]", toString(round(temp$Temp, 1)))
))
```

And a table of tasks becomes a Gantt chart:

```{r}
#| label: gantt
tasks <- data.frame(
  section = c("Setup", "Setup", "Trial", "Trial", "Analysis"),
  task = c("Protocol", "Ethics review", "Recruitment", "Follow-up", "Statistics"),
  days = c(30, 45, 60, 90, 30)
)
# Each task starts when the one before it ends
rows <- sprintf(
  "    %s :t%d, %s, %dd",
  tasks$task, seq_len(nrow(tasks)),
  c("2026-01-05", paste0("after t", seq_len(nrow(tasks) - 1))), tasks$days
)
sections <- split(rows, factor(tasks$section, unique(tasks$section)))
pele(c(
  "gantt",
  "  title Clinical study",
  "  dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD",
  unlist(Map(function(name, rows) c(paste("  section", name), rows), names(sections), sections))
))
```

## More diagram types

pele draws most Mermaid types. A raw string, `r"(...)"`, keeps the Mermaid text as it is written in a `pele` chunk:

```{r}
#| label: mindmap
pele(r"(
mindmap
  root((peler))
    Quarto
      HTML
      PDF
      Word
    R Markdown
    Shiny
    Files
      SVG
      PNG
      PDF
)")
```

```{r}
#| label: quadrant
pele(r"(
quadrantChart
  title Which plot?
  x-axis Low effort --> High effort
  y-axis Low value --> High value
  quadrant-1 Plan it
  quadrant-2 Do it now
  quadrant-3 Skip it
  quadrant-4 Delegate
  Boxplot: [0.2, 0.8]
  Volcano plot: [0.45, 0.9]
  3D pie: [0.7, 0.1]
  Heatmap: [0.75, 0.7]
)")
```

```{r}
#| label: pie
pele(r"(
pie title Time spent on a figure
  "Getting the data" : 45
  "Plotting" : 15
  "Moving the legend" : 40
)")
```

## Files

`pele_save()` picks the format from the file extension:

```r
d <- pele("flowchart LR\n  A --> B")
pele_save(d, "diagram.svg")
pele_save(d, "diagram.png", scale = 2)
pele_save(d, "diagram.pdf")
```

## Shiny

A diagram is HTML, so `renderUI()` is enough. A syntax error shows up in the
output in place of the diagram, with the line and a caret under the mistake.

```r
library(shiny)
library(peler)

ui <- fluidPage(
  textAreaInput("src", NULL, "flowchart LR\n  A --> B", rows = 4),
  uiOutput("diagram")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$diagram <- renderUI(pele(input$src))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

## Colours

Without a theme, a diagram in HTML keeps pele's CSS variables, so the page's
stylesheet sets its colours. This rule makes diagrams follow Quarto's dark mode:

```css
.quarto-dark .pele {
  --pele-bg: #1c1b1a;
  --pele-fg: #e6e4d9;
  --pele-muted: #b7b5ac;
  --pele-line: #cecdc3;
  --pele-surface: #282726;
  --pele-border: #575653;
}
```

`pele_theme()` fixes the colours instead. peler writes them into the SVG and
paints the background, so the diagram looks the same on any page and in any
file. Variables you leave out keep pele's defaults.

```{r}
#| label: flexoki
flexoki <- pele_theme(
  bg = "#fffcf0", fg = "#100f0f", line = "#205ea6",
  surface = "#f2f0e5", border = "#205ea6"
)
pele("flowchart LR\n  A[Mermaid text] --> B[SVG]", theme = flexoki)
```

For every diagram in a document, set the option once:

```r
options(peler.theme = flexoki)
```

A theme can hand single colours back to the page. `"inherit"` takes the page's
value of that pele variable, and a `var()` with a fallback follows any other page
variable. Here the lines and borders stay blue, the text follows Bootstrap's body
colour, and the background comes from the page's `.pele` rule, such as the dark
mode one above:

```r
pele_theme(
  line = "#205ea6",
  border = "#205ea6",
  fg = "var(--bs-body-color, #1f1f1f)",
  bg = "inherit"
)
```

Files have no page, so there `"inherit"` gives pele's default and a `var()` its
fallback.

Fonts are a `pele()` argument and not part of the theme. pele measures labels
in the font to lay out the diagram, so changing the font afterwards would leave the boxes the wrong size.

## Differences from pele in the browser

- **Text widths.** pele measures text with a canvas when it runs in a browser.
V8 has no canvas, so pele estimates widths from Arial metrics. A font much wider than Arial can overflow its boxes.
- **One patched regex.** The V8 engine in the R package is built without ICU,
so it rejects Unicode property escapes such as `\p{L}`. pele uses them once,
to validate font names. `data-raw/update_pele.R` replaces them with a character
range when it vendors the bundle.
- **CSS variables in files.** librsvg, which writes the PNG and PDF files,
ignores CSS variable definitions, so pele's output would come out black. peler
writes the colour values into the SVG before converting it.
- **No `mount()` or zoom.** These need a browser DOM. peler only uses pele's `render()`.
